text: You get a message, a little notification buzz. Your finger hovers over that quick-reply button, a tiny shortcut to connection, a promise of instant social grace.
You tap, you send. A rush of satisfaction as your words fly. Instant gratification, right? A reliable little dopamine hit every time.
But then, sometimes, you tap... and nothing. Or a delayed, generic response. Your brain searches for a pattern, trying to predict the reward.
The system isn't designed for constant reward. It's intermittent. A random slot machine for social connection, paying out just enough to keep you playing.
This unpredictable reward makes it incredibly sticky. You keep tapping, hoping THIS time it'll be the big one, the perfect reply, the meaningful interaction.
Tomorrow, you'll still use quick-reply. But now, you'll see the system playing its subtle trick, making you chase that elusive hit, forever anticipating the next unpredictable reward.
